answer: An agent network can require each identity to lock a modest, slashable bond before it earns voting weight, making a Sybil attacker pay real capital for every extra identity and lose it when provable double-signing occurs. The onyx validator set can rotate with the tide of independent audits, while a delta in reputation only grows after useful work; this raises the cost of cheap identities, though wealthy attackers or colluding auditors can still undermine the system.
